raw_response:
**My thinking, as that farmer:**

I've been working this land for 35 years. I know Quzhou soil — it's sandy loam, dries out fast, and the well is what keeps everything alive. My daughter works in the city now, so it's mostly me and my husband. I can't overextend myself.

Stevia is where the money is. The collection station buys dry leaf every season. I'll keep 3 mu on stevia — that's what I can manage alone for the hand-harvesting. I deep-plough that plot before spring, it needs it. Stevia drinks a lot of water and I pump from the well often through the hot months.

The other 3 mu I do what everyone here does — wheat in winter, maize in summer, same ground, two crops in one year. For wheat I buy the county extension-recommended improved variety, same as last few years, it did fine. For maize I always buy hybrid seed — the local agro-input shop has the one I like. I rotary-till quickly after wheat harvest so I can get maize in fast.

I fertilize by feel from experience, probably a bit more nitrogen than the pamphlets say but I've never had a shortage. I irrigate wheat four times — before sowing, at jointing, heading, and filling. Maize I water at planting, tasseling, and if it gets dry in August. Stevia I water more — whenever the leaves start to look tired.

For pesticides: wheat gets a herbicide pass and a fungicide near heading. Maize gets a herbicide and a spray for corn borer. Stevia I spray three times, mainly for aphids and whitefly.
